newsitem.title: UK: Physical aluminium demand slack, focus on January.
newsitem.headline: Physical aluminium demand slack, focus on January.

text.p: Physical aluminium premiums in Europe remain steady despite slow demand as the market keeps an eye on tight January dates, traders said.
Some expected premiums to ease slightly in coming weeks, reflecting the soggy demand and as metal is sold to take advantage of the January backwardation.

Consumers were still holding back on spot business, waiting for a correction from the rally that had seen three month London Metal Exchange (LME) prices rally about $150 from the October 10 low of $1,305.

"A lot of business is being done for next year but only on a premium basis. There hasn't been a strong level of price fixing, which shows that the perception is the LME is not out of the wood yet," a trader said.
Premiums for Good Western duty unpaid ingots in Rotterdam were quoted little changed at $30/$35, and duty paid unchanged at $110/$120.
A few quotes strayed out of these parameters, with one duty unpaid offer at $40, while a duty paid bid was at $105 and offer at $125.
Part of the reason for the tightness in January had been players putting together consignment stocks and borrowing January-three months for the warrants, a trader said.
"Most of the metal in Rotterdam is in the hands of a very few people and on top of that most of the Western ingots there are in the hands of even fewer people," a trader said.
"This is basically why you have these premiums, they are not being bid up, they are being offered up," he added.
But as January approaches, premiums would likely slip because the tightness would be sold into, another trader said.
An industry source agreed that premiums should drift down, saying, "the big traders are trying to keep premiums firm, but with the slow demand I think they will ease a bit over the next weeks."
Russian off-grade material was scarce, as it had been for some time, with A7 in very short supply. Few trades have been seen and several traders said their quotes were nominal rates.
A7 was quoted slightly higher than two weeks ago, up $5 at $15/$25, with one trader citing offers as high as $35. A6 was put at $5/$10, with one offer higher at $20.
